question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 10
Article 14
Article 5
Article 11
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 11

Explanation:
Article 11 of the Indian Constitution empowers Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law. While Articles 5 to 10 deal with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution, Article 11 gives Parliament the power to make any provision regarding citizenship. Under this article, the Citizenship Act, 1955 was enacted, which provides for acquisition and termination of citizenship. Thus, Article 11 grants legislative power to Parliament on citizenship matters.

☛ Citizenship Act, 1955 → Enacted under Article 11
☛ Articles 5-10 → Deal with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution
☛ Article 10 → Continuance of citizenship
☛ Article 5 → Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution

question: In the three-tier structure of the Panchayati Raj system in India, which body is elected at the grassroots level? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Panchayat Samiti
Gram Panchayat
Zila Parishad
Block Samiti
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Gram Panchayat

Explanation:
In the three-tier structure of the Panchayati Raj system in India, the Gram Panchayat is elected at the grassroots level. It is the smallest unit of local self-government, constituted for one or more villages. Members of Gram Panchayat are directly elected by the rural voters. Its head is called the Sarpanch, who is also directly elected. The Gram Panchayat works on subjects like rural development, sanitation, drinking water, education, and public health. The other two tiers are Panchayat Samiti (block level) and Zila Parishad (district level). The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj system.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What is the head of Gram Panchayat called? → Sarpanch
☛ Which amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj? → 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992
☛ At which level does Panchayat Samiti function? → Block level
☛ Who is the head of Zila Parishad? → Chairperson (elected) or District Collector (nominated)
☛ What is the term of Gram Panchayat? → 5 years
question_hi: भारत में पंचायती राज व्यवस्था की त्रिस्तरीय संरचना में, कौन सी संस्था ग्राम स्तर पर चुनी जाती है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 1)

जिला परिषद

Explanation:

question: Which of the following is NOT an elected position under the Panchayati Raj system in India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Panchayat Secreatary
Zila Pramukh
Sarpanch
Pradhan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Panchayat Secretary

Explanation:
Under the Panchayati Raj system, Sarpanch (village head), Pradhan (chief of Gram Panchayat), and Zila Pramukh (chairperson of Zila Parishad) are directly elected by the people. In contrast, Panchayat Secretary is a gazetted officer appointed by the state government and not elected. This system was formalized under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992). The Panchayat Secretary handles administrative duties and maintains records, while the other three posts are filled through democratic elections.

☛ Chairperson of Zila Parishad is called → Zila Pramukh
☛ Panchayat Secretary is appointed by → State Government
☛ Three tiers of Panchayati Raj → Gram Panchayat, Block Samiti, Zila Parishad

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides a right to profess, practice and propagate religion? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 24
​Article 23
​Article 25
​Article 26
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 25

Explanation:
Article 25 of the Indian Constitution provides the right to profess, practice and propagate religion. It is a fundamental right under Part III and guarantees every person the freedom to adopt, practice and spread any religion of their choice. This right is subject to public order, morality and health. Additionally, the State is empowered to regulate any economic, financial or political activities associated with religious practices. Article 25 lays the foundation of secularism in India, ensuring equal freedom for all religions. It protects individual conscience and allows the propagation of religious beliefs, while also enabling the State to make laws for social welfare and reform, such as prohibiting practices like untouchability or temple entry restrictions.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Right to profess, practice and propagate religion → Article 25
☛ Right to manage religious affairs → Article 26
☛ Secularism is part of basic structure → Kesavananda Bharati case
☛ Article 25 subject to public order, morality and health → Proviso
☛ Freedom of religion is a fundamental right → Part III

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution states about the duty of Union Public Service Commission to present its report annually to the President of India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 324
​Article 321
​Article 322
​Article 323
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 323

Explanation:
Article 323 of the Indian Constitution deals with the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC). It mandates the UPSC to present an annual report of its work to the President of India, who then places it before both Houses of Parliament. This ensures accountability and transparency of the commission. Note that Article 321 deals with additional functions of UPSC, Article 322 with salaries and allowances of members, and Article 324 with the Election Commission. Hence, the duty to submit an annual report is specifically under Article 323.

question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के निम्नलिखित में से किस अनुच्छेद में भारत के राष्ट्रपति को अपनी वार्षिक रिपोर्ट प्रस्तुत करने के संघ लोक सेवा आयोग के कर्तव्य के बारे में बताया गया है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 1)

question: Among, the democratic countries of the world, which country’s constitution is the longest written constitution and most detailed? (RRB NTPC Tier I (22/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: Japan
UK
South Africa
India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is India

Explanation:
India's Constitution is the longest written constitution among all democratic countries in the world. It contains 448 articles, 12 schedules, and more than 100 amendments. The Indian Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950. It was drafted by the Constituent Assembly under the chairmanship of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. It is the most detailed constitution because it incorporates the best provisions from various countries' constitutions. The UK has an unwritten constitution, Japan has a short constitution, and South Africa's constitution is also shorter than India's. Hence, India's constitution is the longest and most detailed.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Adoption of Indian Constitution → 26 November 1949
☛ Chief architect of Indian Constitution → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ Total articles in Indian Constitution → 448
☛ Total schedules in Indian Constitution → 12
☛ Indian Constitution came into effect → 26 January 1950
question_hi: विश्व के लोकतान्त्रिक देशों में से किस देश का संविधान सबसे लंबा लिखित संविधान और सबसे विस्तृत है? (RRB NTPC Tier I (22/04/2016) Shift 2)

यूके
दक्षिण अफ्रीका
भारत
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भारत

Explanation:
भारत का संविधान विश्व के सभी लोकतांत्रिक देशों में सबसे लंबा लिखित संविधान है। इसमें 448 अनुच्छेद, 12 अनुसूचियां और 100 से अधिक संशोधन शामिल हैं। भारत का संविधान 26 नवंबर 1949 को बनकर तैयार हुआ और 26 जनवरी 1950 को लागू हुआ। इसे डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर की अध्यक्षता में संविधान सभा द्वारा तैयार किया गया था। यह विश्व का सबसे विस्तृत संविधान है क्योंकि इसमें विभिन्न देशों के संविधानों से सर्वोत्तम प्रावधानों को सम्मिलित किया गया है। ब्रिटेन का संविधान अलिखित है, जापान का संविधान छोटा है, और दक्षिण अफ्रीका का संविधान भी भारत से छोटा है। इसलिए भारत का संविधान सबसे लंबा और विस्तृत है।

question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental right of an Indian Citizen? (RRB NTPC Tier I (22/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: Right to Equality
Right to Property
Right to freedom of religion
Right against Exploitation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Right to Property

Explanation:
The Right to Property was originally a fundamental right under Article 31 of the Indian Constitution. However, the 44th Amendment Act, 1978, removed it from Part III (Fundamental Rights) and placed it under Article 300A as a constitutional right. The remaining options—Right to Equality (Articles 14-18), Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28), and Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24)—are still fundamental rights under Part III of the Constitution. Thus, the Right to Property is not a fundamental right today.

question: Lieutenant Governor in India ______A. is appointed by the army.B. act as the nominal head of the union territory.C. they are elected by the people of India.D. is accountable to the Council of Ministers of The Chief Minister. (RRB NTPC Tier I (22/04/2016) Shift 3)
options: B
C
A
D
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is B

Explanation:
In India, the Lieutenant Governor acts as the nominal head of a union territory. They are appointed by the President of India, not by the army. The Lieutenant Governor is not elected by the people; rather, they are the representative of the President. They are not accountable to the Chief Minister or the Council of Ministers; instead, they are responsible to the central government. In union territories, the position of Lieutenant Governor is similar to that of a Governor in states, but certain powers remain with the central government. The Lieutenant Governor exercises administrative, legislative, and financial powers subject to the authority of the President.

question: According to the Indian constitution, how many languages have been given the status of official language?A. 15B. 18C. 22D. 25 (RRB NTPC Tier I (28/04/2016) Shift 1)

A
solution:

Explanation:

question: Who presides over the joint sitting of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (29/12/2020) Shift 2)
options: The speaker of the Lok-Sabha
A member nominated by the President of India
The senior most member of the Rajya Sabha
The President of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The speaker of the Lok-Sabha

Explanation:
Under Article 118(4) of the Constitution, the joint sitting of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha is presided over by the Speaker of Lok Sabha. This provision helps resolve deadlocks between the two Houses on a bill. The joint sitting is summoned by the President, but it is chaired by the Lok Sabha Speaker. In the Speaker's absence, the Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha presides. The President is part of Parliament but does not chair joint sittings. This procedure ensures smooth legislative functioning in the Indian parliamentary system.

question: Who is Known as the ‘Father of Indian Constitution’? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (29/12/2020) Shift 2)

question: What was the Government of India Act 1935 based on? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: The principle of a federation and parliamentary system
The acceptance of the idea of a constituent assembly to draft a constitution
The principle of session of the British India provinces
The acceptance of the independence of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The principle of a federation and parliamentary system

Explanation:
The Government of India Act 1935 was a landmark act passed by the British Parliament. It was primarily based on the principle of a federation and parliamentary system. The act introduced provincial autonomy and ended dyarchy in the provinces. However, the federal part was never implemented. The act granted special powers to the Governor. It also served as the foundation for the Indian Constitution, as many provisions of the Indian Constitution were borrowed from this act. Hence, the correct answer is 'The principle of a federation and parliamentary system'.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides provisions for a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: Article 164
Article 118
Article 129
Article 108
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 108

Explanation:
Article 108 of the Indian Constitution provides for a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). It is summoned by the President when a bill passed by one House is pending in the other House for more than six months, is rejected, or both Houses disagree. Decisions are taken by majority of the total membership of both Houses. Only three bills have faced joint sittings so far: Dowry Prohibition Bill (1961), Banking Service Commission Bill (1977), and Prevention of Terrorism Bill (POTA, 2002). Other options: Article 164 deals with appointment of Chief Minister by Governor, Article 118 with rule-making power of Parliament, and Article 129 with Supreme Court being a court of record.

question: Which country has the longest written constitution in the world? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/02/2021) Shift 1)

India
England
France
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is India

Explanation:
The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution in the world. It was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950. The Indian Constitution is inspired by various constitutions, including those of Britain, the USA, and Ireland.

question: What is the meaning of ‘Lokayukta’ in the Constitution of India?  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (22/02/2021) Shift 2)

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is A body operating at the state level to investigate an individual's complaint against public servants or any politician with respect to corruption

Explanation:
In the Indian Constitution, Lokayukta is a state-level institution that investigates complaints against public servants or politicians regarding corruption. This concept was adopted on the recommendation of the Administrative Reforms Commission in 1966. Maharashtra was the first state to establish a Lokayukta. The powers of Lokayukta are wide but subject to judicial review. It plays a crucial role in ensuring transparency and accountability in governance at the state level.
